device.name: Ubiquiti UniFi / EdgeMAX Device (AP / switch / gateway / NVR / NAS)
device.notes:
Ubiquiti UniFi and EdgeMAX infrastructure — access points, switches, gateways/consoles (UDM, Cloud Key), the UniFi NAS and the UniFi Protect NVR (UNVR) — answer the Ubiquiti device-discovery protocol on UDP 10001. This project does NOT implement UniFi control (the inform/adoption protocol and the UniFi Network/OS APIs are out of scope as home infrastructure); we discover the device, pick a pictogram from its platform string, and deep-link to its own admin UI at https://<ip>/.
Ubiquiti discovery: send a broadcast probe to UDP 10001 and devices unicast a TLV reply from port 10001 — they do NOT beacon unsolicited, so the probe is required. Probes: v1 = 01 00 00 00, v2 = 02 08 00 00 (try v1, fall back to v2 for newer gear). Reply header is [version u8][command u8][length u16 BE], then TLVs each [type u8][length u16 BE][value] — note the 1-byte type but 2-byte big-endian length. Known TLVs: 0x01 MAC (6B), 0x02 MAC+IPv4 (10B, once per interface), 0x03 firmware string, 0x0a uptime (u32), 0x0b hostname, 0x0c product/platform name (e.g. "UVC G4 Pro", "ES-10X", "UNVR", "UCKP", "UFP-UAP-B"), 0x14/0x15 model code, 0x16 version (v2), 0x17 adoption state. Pictogram comes from the platform string (0x0c); display name from hostname (0x0b). Ubiquiti gear also emits LLDP.
PICTOGRAM by platform prefix: "UVC*"/doorbell -> handled by the camera spec; "U*-UAP*"/"UAP*"/"U6*"/"U7*" -> wifi-ap; "US*"/"ES*"/"USW*" -> network-switch; "UDM*"/"UCK*"/"UCKP*" -> cloud-key (a console); "UNVR*" -> nvr; "UNAS*" -> nas; "UXG*"/"UGW*" -> router. A consumer sets `pictogram` dynamically from 0x0c; the spec-level default here is wifi-ap (the most common UniFi endpoint), overridden per discovered platform.

credentials.notes: Identify-only: no credential crosses to this app. The UniFi OS admin login is entered by the user at https://<ip>/, which we only link to.

factory_reset.effect: Done at the device (hold its reset button ~10 s) and clears the device's own adoption/config, not anything this app stores. We only identify the device.

methods.description: The device is already on the LAN; discovery is the UDP 10001 probe/response.

steps.action: Broadcast the v1 probe 01 00 00 00 to UDP 10001 (fall back to v2 02 08 00 00).
steps.expect: A TLV reply carrying platform (0x0c), hostname (0x0b), firmware (0x03) and MAC+IP (0x02).

steps.action: Offer the admin link https://<ip>/ (UniFi OS console, or the standalone device page).

setup.notes: Nothing to set up for identification: send the UDP 10001 probe, read the TLVs, choose a pictogram from the platform string and offer the https://<ip>/ admin link. Confidence high: verified live against a large real UniFi/EdgeMAX fleet with the authoritative nmap TLV table.

rejoin.notes: Stays discoverable by the UDP-10001 probe (and LLDP) wherever it sits; identity keys on MAC/hostname, not IP.

testing.notes: Ubiquiti device discovery verified live 2026-08-14: a broadcast probe to 255.255.255.255:10001 (v1 probe 01 00 00 00, v2 02 08 00 00) drew TLV replies from a large real fleet, decoded per the type table — access points bridged into Protect (platform "UFP-UAP-B", hosts "downstairs", "UpstairsU6LR", "BedroomAP"), an EdgeSwitch 10X ("livingroom-switch", model "EdgeSwitch 10X"), a UniFi NAS Pro ("UNASPRO"/"HCBackup"), a UNVR ("UNVR-home") and a Cloud Key Gen2+ ("UCKP"/"cloudkey"). Each carried platform (0x0c), hostname (0x0b), firmware (0x03) and MAC+IP (0x02), confirming the 1-byte-type / 2-byte-length-BE TLV framing and the field mapping. Identify-only: the app shows a pictogram and links to the device's UniFi OS / EdgeMAX admin page. (UniFi Protect cameras from the SAME probe are handled by unifi-protect-camera.yaml.)
